claim_topic: Is ozone suitable for the treatment of tooth decay?
evidence_text: Claim: Is ozone suitable for the treatment of tooth decay? | Finding: Treating caries quickly and painlessly with ozone instead of syringes, drills and fillings - that sounds tempting. However, well-done studies on the efficacy and safety of ozone treatment are lacking. To be sure, there are some positive indications. But they are not enough to recommend ozone therapy for the general public.

claim_topic: Does the so-called blood group diet have any health benefits?
evidence_text: Claim: Does the so-called blood group diet have any health benefits? | Finding: Already the theory of the blood group diet is scientifically implausible. More importantly, there are no conclusive studies that prove any health benefits of this diet.

claim_topic: Can pumpkin seeds or preparations from them help women and men with irritable bladder, bladder weakness or incontinence?
evidence_text: Claim: Can pumpkin seeds or preparations from them help women and men with irritable bladder, bladder weakness or incontinence? | Finding: Whether pumpkin seeds can help has not yet been sufficiently researched.

claim_topic: Do products from bees like honey, propolis, royal jelly or bee venom help against cancer?
evidence_text: Claim: Do products from bees like honey, propolis, royal jelly or bee venom help against cancer? | Finding: So far, only laboratory experiments in the Petri dish and animal studies have been carried out. Studies on cancer patients are still lacking. Therefore, it is currently not possible to assess whether such products are also suitable as a remedy for cancer in humans.

claim_topic: Do pumpkin seed preparations improve symptoms caused by a benign enlarged prostate?
evidence_text: Claim: Do pumpkin seed preparations improve symptoms caused by a benign enlarged prostate? | Finding: In two studies, symptoms did not improve even after one year of treatment.

claim_topic: Can gels and ointments containing arnica, hawthorn, cypress, butcher's broom, Asian (or Indian) pennywort, and heparin, such as VaricoFix, relieve discomfort and secondary symptoms of varicose veins?
evidence_text: Claim: Can gels and ointments containing arnica, hawthorn, cypress, butcher's broom, Asian (or Indian) pennywort, and heparin, such as VaricoFix, relieve discomfort and secondary symptoms of varicose veins? | Finding: There are no good studies on the efficacy of the above-mentioned combination of active ingredients or on individual ingredients of VaricoFix. No scientifically proven statements can be made about possible side effects of the preparation either.

claim_topic: Does putting onion bags help with acute otitis media?
evidence_text: Claim: Does putting onion bags help with acute otitis media? | Finding: There is a lack of good studies on the use of onion bags in children suffering from acute otitis media. Therefore, we cannot make any statements about a possible benefit of this home remedy. However, it can be said that the common ear infections usually heal without complications.

claim_topic: Can serious problems occur after stopping antidepressants?
evidence_text: Claim: Can serious problems occur after stopping antidepressants? | Finding: It is now well documented that discontinuing certain antidepressants can lead to health problems. The symptoms are similar to those experienced when withdrawing from strong tranquilizers.

claim_topic: Does self urine help with health problems?
evidence_text: Claim: Does self urine help with health problems? | Finding: There is not a single health complaint for which there is proof of efficacy of a urine application.

claim_topic: Do unsaturated fats (from plants and fish) reduce cardiovascular disease compared to saturated fats (from meat and dairy products)?
evidence_text: Claim: Do unsaturated fats (from plants and fish) reduce cardiovascular disease compared to saturated fats (from meat and dairy products)? | Finding: Replacing saturated fats more often with unsaturated fats probably reduces the risk of cardiovascular disease.

claim_topic: Is a vegetarian diet including eggs and dairy products healthier than a diet that includes meat?
evidence_text: Claim: Is a vegetarian diet including eggs and dairy products healthier than a diet that includes meat? | Finding: People who eat a vegetarian diet do not seem to live longer than people who eat meat. However, it is possible that the meat-free diet causes them to develop cardiovascular diseases or cancer less frequently.

claim_topic: Can washing hands with antibacterial soaps or wash lotions containing triclosan or triclocarban prevent the risk of contracting diseases in the household?
evidence_text: Claim: Can washing hands with antibacterial soaps or wash lotions containing triclosan or triclocarban prevent the risk of contracting diseases in the household? | Finding: Washing hands clearly protects against infections. However, those who use antibacterial soaps for this purpose are very unlikely to contract infectious diseases any less frequently than people who use conventional soap. This statement applies to soaps containing the active ingredients triclosan or triclocarban. Whether other antibacterial active ingredients in soaps work better has not been investigated.

evidence_text: Claim: Can hand washing with antibacterial soaps or wash lotions containing other disinfectants reduce the risk of infection compared to regular soap??? | Finding: Washing hands clearly protects against infections. claim_topic: Does homeopathy work better than a placebo?
evidence_text: Claim: Does homeopathy work better than a placebo? | Finding: The summarized results of previous studies show: There are no diseases or complaints for which homeopathy has been proven to help better than a placebo.

claim_topic: Does toothpaste containing xylitol reduce the risk of caries?
evidence_text: Claim: Does toothpaste containing xylitol reduce the risk of caries? | Finding: At least in children, xylitol in toothpaste in addition to fluoride could reduce the caries risk. However, reliability is limited by the small number of studies, which were only conducted under very similar conditions and have some methodological shortcomings. Studies on other xylitol-containing products are methodologically flawed and come to contradictory results

claim_topic: Are paper towels or electric dryers more hygienic after washing hands?
evidence_text: Claim: Are paper towels or electric dryers more hygienic after washing hands? | Finding: Studies to date do not allow any clear conclusions to be drawn as to which method most reliably reduces the germ load on the hands. However, the number of studies is also rather poor, since the studies use very different methods and have various shortcomings. The good news is that drying is less important for germ contamination than washing hands beforehand!

claim_topic: Are soy foods risky for people with unremarkable, or subclinical, hypothyroidism?
evidence_text: Claim: Are soy foods risky for people with unremarkable, or subclinical, hypothyroidism? | Finding: Based on the study situation, it is unclear whether foods from soybeans can worsen inconspicuous hypothyroidism in susceptible individuals to the point where symptoms occur. One study does provide some evidence in this direction. But more robust research is needed to better clarify the issue.

claim_topic: Does taking vitamin B3 prolong life?
evidence_text: Claim: Does taking vitamin B3 prolong life? | Finding: At present, only individual laboratory experiments on simple worms indicate that vitamin B3 could have a life-prolonging effect. Whether this also applies to humans is completely unclear; studies on this are lacking.

claim_topic: Can taking Ribose help with heart conditions such as heart failure, narrowing of the coronary arteries (coronary artery disease), or heart attack?
evidence_text: Claim: Can taking Ribose help with heart conditions such as heart failure, narrowing of the coronary arteries (coronary artery disease), or heart attack? | Finding: Some studies do suggest that there may be a possible link between the intake of (D)-ribose and cardiac function. However, these studies are not very conclusive.

claim_topic: Are vitamins and minerals effective and safe in lowering cholesterol?
evidence_text: Claim: Are vitamins and minerals effective and safe in lowering cholesterol? | Finding: Whether dietary supplements can lower cholesterol is still poorly researched. We have answered further questions in separate articles: Multivitamin supplements have not been shown to reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease. It is possible that fish oil capsules have a positive effect, but this must first be confirmed in well-done studies.

claim_topic: Is fasting effective and safe in the long term for arthritis and other diseases?
evidence_text: Claim: Is fasting effective and safe in the long term for arthritis and other diseases? | Finding: It is unclear whether fasting has lasting positive health effects, for example in rheumatoid arthritis. Conclusive studies are lacking. Intensive research is currently being conducted in this field with its many aspects - better studies are in prospect.

claim_topic: Do green smoothies promote health?
evidence_text: Claim: Do green smoothies promote health? | Finding: There are no studies on green smoothies. Neither about effectiveness nor about possible side effects can be scientifically proven statements.

claim_topic: Does chocolate have a mood-lifting effect?
evidence_text: Claim: Does chocolate have a mood-lifting effect? | Finding: Chocolate actually contains many substances that can theoretically influence mood. However, they occur in concentrations that are too low for this. Nevertheless, the sweetness, the expectation and the "overall package chocolate" lead under certain circumstances to an - albeit short-term - improvement in mood.

claim_topic: Do sprouts or buds have a healing effect?
evidence_text: Claim: Do sprouts or buds have a healing effect? | Finding: A healing effect of buds has not been investigated in a single scientific study so far. There is no evidence that ingredients from buds can cure diseases.

claim_topic: Is belly fat or is a large abdominal girth particularly dangerous for health?
evidence_text: Claim: Is belly fat or is a large abdominal girth particularly dangerous for health? | Finding: Current studies suggest that fat deposits in the abdomen ("visceral fat˝) may increase the risk of premature death. It is possible that individuals with unremarkable body mass index are also at risk. In the coming years, new studies will probably allow a better assessment.

claim_topic: Can choline ingested with food - alone or in the form of lecithin, for example - improve memory?
evidence_text: Claim: Can choline ingested with food - alone or in the form of lecithin, for example - improve memory? | Finding: Studies conducted to date provide no clear indication of whether supplemental intake of choline leads to improved memory in healthy people or in people with dementia who are not choline deficient.

claim_topic: Does white sugar cause cancer?
evidence_text: Claim: Does white sugar cause cancer? | Finding: Studies on white sugar cannot be found, but a link between sugar in general and cancer has also not been established.

claim_topic: Do wound care products with sodium hypochlorite such as ActiMaris promote the healing process of wounds?
evidence_text: Claim: Do wound care products with sodium hypochlorite such as ActiMaris promote the healing process of wounds? | Finding: We could not find any high-quality studies that investigated the influence of highly diluted sodium hypochlorite on the healing of chronic wounds. The same applies to fresh wounds and burns. Due to methodological deficiencies, the few existing studies do not allow a statement on efficacy or inefficacy or on possible negative effects of wound care with agents containing sodium hypochlorite.

claim_topic: Does the dietary supplement MSM help with osteoarthritis?
evidence_text: Claim: Does the dietary supplement MSM help with osteoarthritis? | Finding: There are indications of a possible positive effect of MSM in osteoarthritis. However, it is not very well proven to what extent these effects discovered in studies are also noticeable and sustainable in the everyday life of those affected.

claim_topic: Is wheat lectin, which is found in high amounts especially in whole wheat, harmful to health?
evidence_text: Claim: Is wheat lectin, which is found in high amounts especially in whole wheat, harmful to health? | Finding: There are no well-done long-term observations on healthy people from the general population. Therefore, there is a lack of robust data on the benefits and risks of a long-term diet without wheat lectin or whole wheat. However, that a varied diet with whole grains containing lectin protects against some diseases is relatively well established.

claim_topic: Is it harmful to health to regularly eat large quantities of fish contaminated with dioxins and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs)?
evidence_text: Claim: Is it harmful to health to regularly eat large quantities of fish contaminated with dioxins and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs)? | Finding: Salmon and other river and ocean fish often contain traces of toxic dioxins and PCBs. However, too little research has been done to determine whether the amount of these toxins in regular fish consumption is sufficient to endanger health.

claim_topic: Is the DMPS test suitable to reliably indicate mercury poisoning?
evidence_text: Claim: Is the DMPS test suitable to reliably indicate mercury poisoning? | Finding: There are currently no well-done studies with reliable statements on the subject. So it remains open whether the DMPS test really benefits people who suspect heavy metal poisoning. However, risks of DMPS are known. All in all, this diagnostic tool therefore does not appear to be recommendable.

claim_topic: Can stevia lower high blood pressure?
evidence_text: Claim: Can stevia lower high blood pressure? | Finding: With all foods, "the dose makes the poison". As a sugar-free sweetener, substances from the stevia plant do not promote tooth decay and have no calories. A medical benefit beyond that may be an effectiveness against high blood pressure.

claim_topic: Is eating genetically modified corn a health concern?
evidence_text: Claim: Is eating genetically modified corn a health concern? | Finding: Several feeding studies in rats over short periods of time provide no clear indications of a health concern for various genetically modified corn varieties Whether side effects may occur over a longer period of time cannot be answered due to the lack of conclusive long-term studies in humans.

claim_topic: Are privately performed IgG tests to clarify food intolerances meaningful?
evidence_text: Claim: Are privately performed IgG tests to clarify food intolerances meaningful? | Finding: Whether elevated levels of immunoglobulin G in the blood are actually signs of intolerance to certain foods is highly controversial. Studies in which people with intestinal diseases avoid specific foods provide no clear evidence of benefit.

claim_topic: Is a gluten-free diet recommended for people who do not have celiac disease?
evidence_text: Claim: Is a gluten-free diet recommended for people who do not have celiac disease? | Finding: There are no well-done studies that have investigated gluten abstinence in people who do not suffer from the autoimmune disease celiac disease. Therefore, there is a lack of reliable data on the possible benefits of a long-term gluten-free diet in the general population. Equally poorly studied are any risks of this form of renunciation, which is so hip at the moment.

claim_topic: Does the plant substance nobiletin contained in mandarins protect against weight gain?
evidence_text: Claim: Does the plant substance nobiletin contained in mandarins protect against weight gain? | Finding: In genetically modified laboratory mice, the additional administration of nobiletin to a high-fat and high-sugar diet appears to be able to prevent obesity. Such an effect has not yet been studied in humans.

claim_topic: Does consumption of dairy products in middle and advanced age protect against bone fractures?
evidence_text: Claim: Does consumption of dairy products in middle and advanced age protect against bone fractures? | Finding: Those who are 40 or older and consume a lot of dairy products do not seem to be able to reduce their risk of age-related bone fractures.

claim_topic: Is the milk of horn-bearing cows less rich in allergens and more easily tolerated by lactose-intolerant individuals?
evidence_text: Claim: Is the milk of horn-bearing cows less rich in allergens and more easily tolerated by lactose-intolerant individuals? | Finding: There is no well-done study that would provide conclusive scientific evidence to support these questions.

claim_topic: Does daily flossing protect against tooth decay, periodontitis and tooth loss?
evidence_text: Claim: Does daily flossing protect against tooth decay, periodontitis and tooth loss? | Finding: It is possible that regular flossing of the interdental spaces can help with mild gingivitis. However, there are no good studies that investigate whether this has a preventive effect against inflammation in healthy gums. The effect on the development of plaque is unclear. There are no studies at all on the question of whether flossing leads to fewer cavities, periodontitis or tooth loss.

claim_topic: Do protein supplements help build muscle?
evidence_text: Claim: Do protein supplements help build muscle? | Finding: A lot of research is being done in the field. However, the studies often have methodological flaws and contradictory results. It is therefore currently unclear whether and in what form supplemental proteins can help on the way to a six-pack and biceps.

claim_topic: Does music therapy promote recovery from severe limitations of consciousness after severe brain injury?
evidence_text: Claim: Does music therapy promote recovery from severe limitations of consciousness after severe brain injury? | Finding: We have not found any high-quality studies that specifically investigate the effect of music therapy. Some scientists explored the influence of stimulation of the senses, in which acoustic stimuli are also used. However, since these studies followed only a few people over short periods of time and had many methodological problems, they do not allow us to draw any firm conclusions.

claim_topic: Can eating grapefruit in combination with some medications lead to harmful interactions?
evidence_text: Claim: Can eating grapefruit in combination with some medications lead to harmful interactions? | Finding: Yes, grapefruits can enhance the effects of some medications. However, the risk, type, and severity of side effects are only partially known, depend on the particular drug, and likely vary from person to person.

claim_topic: Can regular consumption of chocolate prevent cardiovascular disease?
evidence_text: Claim: Can regular consumption of chocolate prevent cardiovascular disease? | Finding: It is possible, but by no means certain, that chocolate could reduce the risk of developing cardiovascular disease such as heart attack or stroke. However, the high proportion of sugar and fat in most types of chocolate could also have negative effects.

claim_topic: Is barley grass good for health?
evidence_text: Claim: Is barley grass good for health? | Finding: Only one small study has tested barley grass extract in humans to date. Barley grass juice has not been studied. The foundations are lacking for a reliable statement.

claim_topic: Are diets with reduced carbohydrate content better for weight loss than other weight loss programs?
evidence_text: Claim: Are diets with reduced carbohydrate content better for weight loss than other weight loss programs? | Finding: There is much evidence to suggest that, in the case of obesity, low-carbohydrate diets lead to at least comparable weight loss over one to two years as fat-reduced diets or weight-loss programs with a balanced diet.

claim_topic: Does taking probiotics during pregnancy and early life protect children from atopic dermatitis?
evidence_text: Claim: Does taking probiotics during pregnancy and early life protect children from atopic dermatitis? | Finding: Current studies suggest that the intake of probiotics could counteract the development of atopic dermatitis. However, many questions about efficacy and intake remain unanswered.

claim_topic: Is Bulletproof Coffee recommended?
evidence_text: Claim: Is Bulletproof Coffee recommended? | Finding: Bulletproof coffee is high in caffeine and fat. Is the hip breakfast substitute a kind of fitness potion? Or is it even harmful? Because there have been no studies on this coffee blend with human test subjects, we cannot make any reliable statements.

claim_topic: Do apples help with smoking cessation?
evidence_text: Claim: Do apples help with smoking cessation? | Finding: Apples contain numerous ingredients and rightly have the reputation of being a healthy snack. Whether they can help to give up cigarettes has not yet been investigated in studies.

claim_topic: Do products made from fenugreek seeds help you lose weight?
evidence_text: Claim: Do products made from fenugreek seeds help you lose weight? | Finding: We found only one study in which participants had not lost weight after six weeks. However, the study period is very short, the number of participants small and the quality mediocre. It therefore remains unclear whether fenugreek seeds can help lose weight in the longer term.

claim_topic: Does skipping breakfast increase heart attack risk?
evidence_text: Claim: Does skipping breakfast increase heart attack risk? | Finding: There is no clear evidence that not eating breakfast could be a cause of obesity and, as a consequence, an increased risk of heart attack. It is possible, however, that it is primarily those people who are overweight and have a higher heart risk who forgo their morning meal.

claim_topic: Does wheat make you fat and sick?
evidence_text: Claim: Does wheat make you fat and sick? | Finding: There is no evidence in current studies that wheat has a special connection with obesity and its consequences. Attributing a special role to wheat seems implausible.

claim_topic: Do whole grains lower the likelihood of dying early?
evidence_text: Claim: Do whole grains lower the likelihood of dying early? | Finding: People who eat whole grain products instead of foods made from refined flour are likely to live longer and probably have a lower risk of dying from cancer or cardiovascular disease.

claim_topic: Does the consumption of dairy products promote mucus and diseases of the ear, nose and throat?
evidence_text: Claim: Does the consumption of dairy products promote mucus and diseases of the ear, nose and throat? | Finding: There is no scientific evidence to prove that cow's milk causes mucus.

claim_topic: Does regular consumption of energy drinks harm heart health?
evidence_text: Claim: Does regular consumption of energy drinks harm heart health? | Finding: This question is insufficiently researched. Larger studies over a longer period of time are needed to assess the heart risk from energy drinks.

claim_topic: Do light drinks promote obesity?
evidence_text: Claim: Do light drinks promote obesity? | Finding: Several cohort studies show that people who frequently drink light drinks are more likely to be overweight. However, this does not prove that sweetener drinks make you fat. For it is equally conceivable that overweight people try to lose weight with light drinks. Whether they are successful in doing so is unclear.

claim_topic: Does coffee reduce the risk of dementia?
evidence_text: Claim: Does coffee reduce the risk of dementia? | Finding: One to two cups of coffee a day may protect against mental decline in the long term. It should not be more than that. It is unclear where this effect comes from and whether other caffeinated beverages might also be protective.

claim_topic: Does sugar consumption increase the risk of developing type 2 diabetes regardless of obesity?
evidence_text: Claim: Does sugar consumption increase the risk of developing type 2 diabetes regardless of obesity? | Finding: Sugar-containing soft drinks can - if consumed regularly - cause obesity. Obesity, in turn, increases the likelihood of developing type 2 diabetes. However, sugared soft drinks probably also increase the risk of diabetes independently of obesity.

claim_topic: Does a lower salt diet reduce the likelihood of cardiovascular disease?
evidence_text: Claim: Does a lower salt diet reduce the likelihood of cardiovascular disease? | Finding: A lower-salt diet has been shown to help reduce elevated blood pressure somewhat. It is possible, but not certain, that this reduces the likelihood of dying from a stroke or the consequences of narrowed heart vessels, such as a heart attack.

claim_topic: Is less eaten from red plates?
evidence_text: Claim: Is less eaten from red plates? | Finding: In two psychological experiments, participants were less likely to eat salty pretzels, popcorn or chocolate chips if they were served on red plates. It is unclear whether the effect lasts over a longer period of time.

claim_topic: Does red wine protect better against cardiovascular disease than white wine?
evidence_text: Claim: Does red wine protect better against cardiovascular disease than white wine? | Finding: There is evidence that moderate amounts of alcohol may protect against cardiovascular disease, but the effect is not well established. Whether this possibly protective effect is stronger with red wine than with white wine or other alcoholic beverages has not been sufficiently investigated.

claim_topic: Do azo food dyes cause attention deficit disorder and hyperactivity in children?
evidence_text: Claim: Do azo food dyes cause attention deficit disorder and hyperactivity in children? | Finding: Some studies fuel the suspicion that azo dyes can exacerbate ADHD symptoms.

claim_topic: Does turmeric prevent or cure cancer?
evidence_text: Claim: Does turmeric prevent or cure cancer? | Finding: Animal studies provide tentative evidence that turmeric can prevent or treat cancer. Whether turmeric has such an effect in humans cannot be assessed due to the low confidence level of a few studies conducted to date.

claim_topic: Does breastfeeding reduce the risk of sudden infant death syndrome?
evidence_text: Claim: Does breastfeeding reduce the risk of sudden infant death syndrome? | Finding: Breastfeeding can possibly reduce the risk of sudden infant death syndrome, but this is not entirely certain. Other factors can also reduce the risk.

claim_topic: Do boron preparations such as borax, boric acid, or calcium fructoborate relieve pain associated with age-related joint wear (osteoarthritis)?
evidence_text: Claim: Do boron preparations such as borax, boric acid, or calcium fructoborate relieve pain associated with age-related joint wear (osteoarthritis)? | Finding: The few studies on this are of poor quality and therefore not trustworthy. Moreover, there is no evidence that the human body needs boron at all.

claim_topic: Can glutamate in food cause intolerance symptoms?
evidence_text: Claim: Can glutamate in food cause intolerance symptoms? | Finding: There is no conclusive evidence that the consumption of glutamate triggers complaints. However, since studies conducted to date have shown deficiencies, it cannot be ruled out that there are isolated individuals who react sensitively to large amounts of glutamate.

claim_topic: Does the Orthopulse device accelerate the orthodontic correction of malocclusions?
evidence_text: Claim: Does the Orthopulse device accelerate the orthodontic correction of malocclusions? | Finding: Poorly done studies show that the device can accelerate tooth movement in the short term. Whether this reduces the overall treatment time has not yet been sufficiently proven. The methodological weaknesses of the studies also mean that the results are not very credible. Possible side effects have not yet been sufficiently investigated.

claim_topic: Is it harmful for the mental development of the unborn child if the mother regularly eats fish contaminated with mercury during pregnancy?
evidence_text: Claim: Is it harmful for the mental development of the unborn child if the mother regularly eats fish contaminated with mercury during pregnancy? | Finding: Many commercially available types of edible fish are contaminated with traces of methyl mercury. There are indications that regular consumption of such mercury-containing fish during pregnancy can impair the brain development of unborn children and thus their later mental abilities. In contrast, consumption of fish low in mercury could promote brain development in the unborn.

claim_topic: Can the consumption of caffeine during pregnancy harm the unborn child?
evidence_text: Claim: Can the consumption of caffeine during pregnancy harm the unborn child? | Finding: There is insufficient evidence that moderate consumption of caffeinated beverages would have a negative impact on the child's development. Up to three cups of coffee a day does not appear to reduce the child's birth weight. Very large amounts of caffeine-containing beverages could possibly contribute to lower birth weight.

claim_topic: Are vegetables prepared in a microwave oven less healthy than those prepared in other ways?
evidence_text: Claim: Are vegetables prepared in a microwave oven less healthy than those prepared in other ways? | Finding: How vegetables change during preparation is extremely variable. With any type of heating, ingredients can be lost or become more easily accessible. In sum, it cannot be said that preparation in the microwave is always a bad choice.

claim_topic: Can garlic extract reduce high blood pressure and thus the risk of cardiovascular disease?
evidence_text: Claim: Can garlic extract reduce high blood pressure and thus the risk of cardiovascular disease? | Finding: Studies to date provide tentative evidence of a blood pressure-lowering effect of garlic. However, they are of too low quality to be able to prove a reduction in the risk of cardiovascular disease as a result of high blood pressure.

claim_topic: Can fructose damage the liver?
evidence_text: Claim: Can fructose damage the liver? | Finding: There is no conclusive evidence for a possible liver-damaging effect of fructose.

claim_topic: Can green tea affect the likelihood of dying early and reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease?
evidence_text: Claim: Can green tea affect the likelihood of dying early and reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease? | Finding: There is a lack of conclusive studies on the health effects of specific matcha. However, there is some evidence that green tea in general may reduce the likelihood of dying prematurely, especially from cardiovascular disease.

claim_topic: Is matcha tea particularly healthy?
evidence_text: Claim: Is matcha tea particularly healthy? | Finding: There is a lack of conclusive studies on the health effects of specific matcha. However, there is some evidence that green tea in general may reduce the likelihood of dying prematurely, especially from cardiovascular disease.

claim_topic: Can acupuncture prevent migraines and tension headaches?
evidence_text: Claim: Can acupuncture prevent migraines and tension headaches? | Finding: In the case of migraine, the preventive effect of acupuncture is probably similar to that of prophylactic medication. However, for both migraine and tension headaches, acupuncture performs only slightly better than sham acupuncture. Whether the pricking of traditional acupuncture points plays a role is unclear.

claim_topic: Can green tea reduce the likelihood of dying from cancer ?
evidence_text: Claim: Can green tea reduce the likelihood of dying from cancer ? | Finding: The results of previous studies suggest that green tea cannot reduce the risk of dying from cancer.

claim_topic: Can plant sterols or foods with them reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease?
evidence_text: Claim: Can plant sterols or foods with them reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease? | Finding: Plant sterols do lower cholesterol levels. However, whether they also reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease has not been researched. Animal studies even provide evidence that plant sterols in large quantities could increase the risk of cardiovascular disease. Whether this also applies to humans has not been investigated.

claim_topic: Can too much iodine cause autoimmune thyroid disease and consequently hypothyroidism?
evidence_text: Claim: Can too much iodine cause autoimmune thyroid disease and consequently hypothyroidism? | Finding: Autoimmune thyroid disease appears to occur more frequently in individuals with high iodine consumption. Whether high levels of iodine actually cause this disease has not been conclusively determined.

claim_topic: Is the sweetener aspartame harmful to health?
evidence_text: Claim: Is the sweetener aspartame harmful to health? | Finding: Health damage from aspartame is unlikely. This also applies to people who consume aspartame-sweetened foods and beverages in large quantities over a long period of time. However, in people suffering from the hereditary disease phenylketonuria (PKU), aspartame can cause nerve and brain damage.

claim_topic: Does coffee affect cancer death risk?
evidence_text: Claim: Does coffee affect cancer death risk? | Finding: Current evidence suggests that coffee consumption in general is neither protective nor detrimental to cancer death risk.

claim_topic: Do diets with primarily or exclusively uncooked foods have health benefits?
evidence_text: Claim: Do diets with primarily or exclusively uncooked foods have health benefits? | Finding: In studies, we have not been able to find convincing evidence that raw foods provide health benefits over healthy diets that include cooked foods. On the contrary, there is also evidence of possible harm.

claim_topic: Can increased water consumption prevent migraines or other headaches?
evidence_text: Claim: Can increased water consumption prevent migraines or other headaches? | Finding: Whether drinking more water can prevent headaches cannot be answered satisfactorily on the basis of studies conducted to date. If there is an effect, however, it is likely to be very small.

claim_topic:
Offer the following herbal appetite suppressants effective and safe weight loss support:
Devil's Tongue (Konjac Root), Caralluma fimbriata, Garcinia cambogia, Gymnea sylvestre, Ephedra, Irvinia gabonensis, Fenugreek, Hoodia gordonii, Common Bean, Bitter Orange?
evidence_text:
Claim: Offer the following herbal appetite suppressants effective and safe weight loss support:
Devil's Tongue (Konjac Root), Caralluma fimbriata, Garcinia cambogia, Gymnea sylvestre, Ephedra, Irvinia gabonensis, Fenugreek, Hoodia gordonii, Common Bean, Bitter Orange? | Finding: Due to the number of studies, it is unclear for a number of supposedly appetite-suppressing dietary supplements whether they can support successful weight loss. Well-done studies that run over a long period of time with a sufficient number of test subjects are scarce. Evidence for long-term safety and simultaneous efficacy is therefore lacking.

claim_topic: Are there health benefits to screening the general population for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) as a precaution?
evidence_text: Claim: Are there health benefits to screening the general population for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) as a precaution? | Finding: Even people with moderately severe COPD may have little health benefit from starting treatment as early as possible. People without symptoms who are diagnosed with COPD only as a result of a screening test are therefore unlikely to gain much health benefit from drug treatment.

claim_topic: Can cow's milk cause iron deficiency in babies in the first year of life?
evidence_text: Claim: Can cow's milk cause iron deficiency in babies in the first year of life? | Finding: Cow's milk is low in usable iron. Therefore, cow's milk appears to increase the likelihood of iron deficiency in the blood of babies. It is unclear whether animal milk increases the risk of type 1 diabetes or blood in the stool, or reduces the likelihood of allergic diseases.

claim_topic: Does cow's milk for babies have other health disadvantages??
evidence_text: Claim: Does cow's milk for babies have other health disadvantages?? | Finding: Cow's milk is low in usable iron. Therefore, cow's milk appears to increase the likelihood of iron deficiency in the blood of babies. It is unclear whether animal milk increases the risk of type 1 diabetes or blood in the stool, or reduces the likelihood of allergic diseases.

claim_topic: Does drinking breast milk as a baby have a positive effect on later health and development?
evidence_text: Claim: Does drinking breast milk as a baby have a positive effect on later health and development? | Finding: It is possible that children who have been exclusively breastfed for a long time are somewhat less likely to become overweight later on. There is also evidence that their IQ is slightly higher. However, it is difficult to isolate the influence of breast milk drinking. Therefore, it is questionable what significance the effects found have in practice.

claim_topic: Does Almased help with excess weight better than other diets?
evidence_text: Claim: Does Almased help with excess weight better than other diets? | Finding: Those who reduce their calorie intake with the help of Almased lose weight. However, whether the product facilitates a diet or works better than other diets is not sufficiently studied.

claim_topic: Do products with talc, such as baby powder, increase the risk of ovarian cancer?
evidence_text: Claim: Do products with talc, such as baby powder, increase the risk of ovarian cancer? | Finding: Basically, cohort studies are more informative than case-control studies. The two existing large cohort studies speak against an increased risk, almost all case-control studies for an increased risk. In order not to underestimate a possible risk, we assess the study situation as unclear despite the cohort studies.

claim_topic: Do large portions, large plates or glasses, and larger packaging cause us to eat and drink more?
evidence_text: Claim: Do large portions, large plates or glasses, and larger packaging cause us to eat and drink more? | Finding: The results of previous studies show that people generally seem to eat more and drink more (non-alcoholic) beverages when they are served larger portions. Whether smaller portions prevent obesity in the long term, however, has not been researched.

claim_topic: Does taking coconut oil improve mental abilities in dementia like Alzheimer's disease?
evidence_text: Claim: Does taking coconut oil improve mental abilities in dementia like Alzheimer's disease? | Finding: We could find only one clinical study on the use of coconut oil in Alzheimer's disease. This was of such poor quality that no firm statement is possible.

claim_topic: Does the preparation "CAPS immu" from Ringana reduce the risk of infections in healthy people?
evidence_text: Claim: Does the preparation "CAPS immu" from Ringana reduce the risk of infections in healthy people? | Finding: Neither for the preparation itself nor for the individual components has such an effect been proven in clinical studies according to our research.

claim_topic: Do extracts from grape seeds have a health-promoting effect?
evidence_text: Claim: Do extracts from grape seeds have a health-promoting effect? | Finding: The quality of studies available to date is too poor and the results are too contradictory to assess whether grape seed extract has a health-promoting effect.

claim_topic: Is the administration of magnesium through the skin effective?
evidence_text: Claim: Is the administration of magnesium through the skin effective? | Finding: There are no well-done studies on this subject. Therefore, we lack reliable information as to whether or in what form magnesium can possibly penetrate the skin and then also have a (desired) effect.

claim_topic: Do kava kava supplements help with anxiety disorders?
evidence_text: Claim: Do kava kava supplements help with anxiety disorders? | Finding: The fact that kava kava may slightly alleviate symptoms of an anxiety disorder is only weakly supported by studies. In addition, several cases of severe liver damage from preparations made from it are known in Europe and the USA.

claim_topic: Do ultrasound devices help against dust mites?
evidence_text: Claim: Do ultrasound devices help against dust mites? | Finding: Only dubiously published studies exist, the quality and significance of which cannot be assessed. Consequently, the effectiveness of the ultrasound devices is unclear.

claim_topic: Does the risk of food allergy decrease if babies are fed potentially allergenic foods (cow's milk, peanuts, chicken egg) as late as possible for the first time?
evidence_text: Claim: Does the risk of food allergy decrease if babies are fed potentially allergenic foods (cow's milk, peanuts, chicken egg) as late as possible for the first time? | Finding: in none of the clinical studies to date has the risk of food allergy decreased by feeding these foods as late as possible. Whether early supplementary feeding can reduce the risk is less clear, but possible at least for peanut allergy. For fish, sesame and wheat, there is only one study, the results of which need to be confirmed in further studies.

claim_topic: for fish, sesame, wheat?
evidence_text: Claim: for fish, sesame, wheat? | Finding: in none of the clinical studies to date has the risk of food allergy decreased by feeding these foods as late as possible. Whether early supplementary feeding can reduce the risk is less clear, but possible at least for peanut allergy. For fish, sesame and wheat, there is only one study, the results of which need to be confirmed in further studies.

claim_topic: Can willow bark tea help with inflammation, pain or fever?
evidence_text: Claim: Can willow bark tea help with inflammation, pain or fever? | Finding: Significant, well-conducted studies are lacking on the effects of willow bark tea on pain, inflammation, or fever.

claim_topic: Can a supposedly "high acid" diet weaken bones?
evidence_text: Claim: Can a supposedly "high acid" diet weaken bones? | Finding: It is not likely that a supposedly "acid-rich" diet weakens the bones. There are no scientific studies on the effect on other diseases.

claim_topic: Does a supposedly "alkaline-rich" diet prevent chronic diseases?
evidence_text: Claim: Does a supposedly "alkaline-rich" diet prevent chronic diseases? | Finding: It is not likely that a supposedly "acid-rich" diet weakens the bones. There are no scientific studies on the effect on other diseases.

claim_topic: Can a blood test detect mental illness?
evidence_text: Claim: Can a blood test detect mental illness? | Finding: Stress can certainly affect blood values, but conversely, we are not aware of any blood test that is actually useful for diagnosing mental illness.

claim_topic: Is surgery for an anterior cruciate ligament tear (by replacing the broken anterior cruciate ligament with tendon tissue from another part of the leg) followed by physical therapy better than physical therapy alone?
evidence_text: Claim: Is surgery for an anterior cruciate ligament tear (by replacing the broken anterior cruciate ligament with tendon tissue from another part of the leg) followed by physical therapy better than physical therapy alone? | Finding: No differences are found between the two treatment methods after either two or five years. However, this should be viewed with great caution. In a study on this, many patients in the group with physiotherapy had surgery after all within the next five years.

claim_topic: Can motherwort reduce migraine attacks?
evidence_text: Claim: Can motherwort reduce migraine attacks? | Finding: The existing studies differ greatly in their methods and the results are sometimes contradictory. According to the study with the most participants, motherwort can slightly reduce the number of migraine attacks per month.

claim_topic: Does metal in bed disturb sleep?
evidence_text: Claim: Does metal in bed disturb sleep? | Finding: Again and again consumers hear that bedsteads made of certain metals or with metal parts are harmful to health. But scientific studies on this are lacking. For this reason, we cannot say whether metal beds change the electrosmog exposure and thus perhaps even have a negative impact on health. From today's point of view, however, a clear danger does not seem particularly likely.

claim_topic: Does heat treatment (radiofrequency ablation or radiofrequency heat ablation of benign nodules of the thyroid gland work as well as conventional surgical methods?
evidence_text: Claim: Does heat treatment (radiofrequency ablation or radiofrequency heat ablation of benign nodules of the thyroid gland work as well as conventional surgical methods? | Finding: It is currently not clear whether this method achieves the same success as conventional surgical methods. The quality of the studies found is poor and leaves many questions about the effectiveness of the method unanswered. Possible undesirable side effects and long-term consequences are also unknown.

claim_topic: Does Imunoglukan strengthen the immune system?
evidence_text: Claim: Does Imunoglukan strengthen the immune system? | Finding: There are no studies that attest to Imunoglukan having a specific effect on a specific disease, nor any that confirm a general immune-boosting effect. The existing studies have glaring deficiencies.

claim_topic: Do cell phones promote the development and growth of tumors in the head?
evidence_text: Claim: Do cell phones promote the development and growth of tumors in the head? | Finding: Despite intensive research, it is currently still unclear whether cell phones promote tumor diseases. According to current knowledge, the risk increases only minimally, if at all.

claim_topic: Does wearing bras promote breast cancer risk?
evidence_text: Claim: Does wearing bras promote breast cancer risk? | Finding: The extent to which wearing bras affects breast cancer risk is poorly understood. So far, results of case-control studies tend to argue against a risk from bras, and there is no serious evidence that bras increase the risk.

claim_topic: Are tattoo inks harmful to health?
evidence_text: Claim: Are tattoo inks harmful to health? | Finding: Many tattoo inks contain substances that are harmful to health. Which colors can be used for tattoos without health concerns is unclear. There are no studies that investigate the risk.

claim_topic: Do plant hormones (phytoestrogens) other than genistein reduce the number and intensity of hot flashes during menopause?
evidence_text: Claim: Do plant hormones (phytoestrogens) other than genistein reduce the number and intensity of hot flashes during menopause? | Finding: It is unclear whether phytoestrogens can help with hot flashes. Studies on this topic are often of modest quality; usually a comparison of the data is not possible. Therefore, an overall judgment cannot be made. One exception is the phytoestrogen genistein. There are indications that this plant substance in higher doses may be able to reduce the number of daily hot flashes a little.

claim_topic: Does the herbal hormone genistein reduce the number and intensity of hot flashes during menopause???
evidence_text: Claim: Does the herbal hormone genistein reduce the number and intensity of hot flashes during menopause??? | Finding: It is unclear whether phytoestrogens can help with hot flashes. Studies on this topic are often of modest quality; usually a comparison of the data is not possible. Therefore, an overall judgment cannot be made. One exception is the phytoestrogen genistein. There are indications that this plant substance in higher doses may be able to reduce the number of daily hot flashes a little.

claim_topic: Does bloodletting according to Hildegard von Bingen have health benefits?
evidence_text: Claim: Does bloodletting according to Hildegard von Bingen have health benefits? | Finding: Traditional bloodletting is based on ideas that have long been disproved and is not the subject of studies. However, in the case of very specific blood diseases, bloodletting is also used in scientific medicine.

claim_topic: Can FGXpress Power Strips reduce pain or improve wound healing?
evidence_text: Claim: Can FGXpress Power Strips reduce pain or improve wound healing? | Finding: We could not find a single study on these patches - nor any reason to assume that they are effective.

claim_topic: Does treatment according to the fascial distortion model help with chronic shoulder pain?
evidence_text: Claim: Does treatment according to the fascial distortion model help with chronic shoulder pain? | Finding: Currently, there is only one randomized controlled trial of this type of therapy. It suggests that fascia therapy may help with some shoulder conditions.

claim_topic: Are there effective alternatives to the breathing mask (CPAP) for sleep apnea?
evidence_text: Claim: Are there effective alternatives to the breathing mask (CPAP) for sleep apnea? | Finding: Although numerous other forms of treatment are available, some of them are too little researched or are clearly inferior to the standard therapy with CPAP.

claim_topic: Does closure of the foramen ovale prevent further strokes in people who have had a stroke of unknown cause?
evidence_text: Claim: Does closure of the foramen ovale prevent further strokes in people who have had a stroke of unknown cause? | Finding: According to three large studies, closure of the patent foramen ovale can prevent another stroke better than purely drug treatment can.

claim_topic: Does stimulation current therapy (TENS - Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation) help with worn knee joints (knee osteoarthritis)?
evidence_text: Claim: Does stimulation current therapy (TENS - Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation) help with worn knee joints (knee osteoarthritis)? | Finding: Whether TENS treatments can improve pain associated with knee osteoarthritis is unclear. In any case, it does not seem to be able to improve restrictions in everyday movements.

claim_topic: Does taking magnesium salts decrease the frequency and intensity of muscle cramps with unknown cause?
evidence_text: Claim: Does taking magnesium salts decrease the frequency and intensity of muscle cramps with unknown cause? | Finding: No high-quality studies have been found on the efficacy of magnesium salts for exercise-induced muscle cramps, such as in athletes. For leg muscle cramps without an identifiable cause, researchers have been unable to demonstrate any effect of magnesium beyond placebo in studies. Pregnant women may benefit from magnesium supplements, but this evidence is not very robust.

claim_topic: Does taking magnesium salts reduce the frequency and intensity of exercise-induced muscle cramps during sports?
evidence_text: Claim: Does taking magnesium salts reduce the frequency and intensity of exercise-induced muscle cramps during sports? | Finding: No high-quality studies have been found on the efficacy of magnesium salts for exercise-induced muscle cramps, such as in athletes. For leg muscle cramps without an identifiable cause, researchers have been unable to demonstrate any effect of magnesium beyond placebo in studies. Pregnant women may benefit from magnesium supplements, but this evidence is not very robust.

claim_topic: Does taking magnesium salts reduce the frequency and intensity of muscle cramps in pregnancy?
evidence_text: Claim: Does taking magnesium salts reduce the frequency and intensity of muscle cramps in pregnancy? | Finding: No high-quality studies have been found on the efficacy of magnesium salts for exercise-induced muscle cramps, such as in athletes. For leg muscle cramps without an identifiable cause, researchers have been unable to demonstrate any effect of magnesium beyond placebo in studies. Pregnant women may benefit from magnesium supplements, but this evidence is not very robust.

claim_topic: Does the active ingredient rivaroxaban (drug Xarelto) have a higher risk of dangerous bleeding than other anticoagulants?
evidence_text: Claim: Does the active ingredient rivaroxaban (drug Xarelto) have a higher risk of dangerous bleeding than other anticoagulants? | Finding: High-quality studies in the most common uses of rivaroxaban show either an equal or even lower risk of bleeding than other blood-clotting medications. However, this does not mean it is the best choice in all cases. Research is still needed for bleeding in the stomach or intestines.

claim_topic: Does vitamin D protect against dementia or memory loss?
evidence_text: Claim: Does vitamin D protect against dementia or memory loss? | Finding: Some studies suggest a possible connection between the vitamin D concentration in the blood and a deteriorating memory or dementia.  Whether vitamin D actually protects against memory deterioration or dementia remains open.

claim_topic: Does brain training boost intelligence?
evidence_text: Claim: Does brain training boost intelligence? | Finding: There are many ways of brain training, but no evidence that it can improve intelligence. The most research in science is about a specific training of the "working memory", here the studies speak against a general improvement of intelligence.

claim_topic: Does petroleum help against cancer?
evidence_text: Claim: Does petroleum help against cancer? | Finding: This rather absurd assumption has not been tested in studies. Since petroleum is more likely to pose a health hazard, such studies are also not conducted.

claim_topic: Does lavender scent help with sleep disorders?
evidence_text: Claim: Does lavender scent help with sleep disorders? | Finding: Based on the state of studies, it is unclear whether inhaling lavender aroma can help with sleep disorders. Most of the currently available studies have gross methodological flaws. In addition, it is uncertain what undesirable side effects may result from (long-term) inhalation of lavender aroma.

claim_topic: Does the drug Sovaldi (sofosbuvir) enable high cure rates for chronic hepatitis C?
evidence_text: Claim: Does the drug Sovaldi (sofosbuvir) enable high cure rates for chronic hepatitis C? | Finding: Yes, in combination with drugs that have been available for some time, cure rates of over 90 percent are possible with sofosbuvir. However, there are many different patient groups, and success rates are not the same for all.

claim_topic: Does alpha lipoic acid help prevent or treat Alzheimer's disease?
evidence_text: Claim: Does alpha lipoic acid help prevent or treat Alzheimer's disease? | Finding: It remains to be seen whether alpha lipoic acid can help prevent or delay the onset of Alzheimer's disease. There is also a lack of conclusive studies on the question of the extent to which the substance can favorably influence the course of a disease that has already broken out.

claim_topic: Are Vemma products good for health?
evidence_text: Claim: Are Vemma products good for health? | Finding: We have found only one study that investigates health effects of Vemma. However, the study is so flawed that it does not allow us to draw any conclusions.

claim_topic: Do over-the-counter cough medicines relieve cough symptoms?
evidence_text: Claim: Do over-the-counter cough medicines relieve cough symptoms? | Finding: That over-the-counter cough medicines provide relief from acute cough is neither proven nor disproven - there are simply no studies of sufficient quality to answer this question.

claim_topic: Does a diet rich in vitamin K2 protect against diseases of the cardiovascular system?
evidence_text: Claim: Does a diet rich in vitamin K2 protect against diseases of the cardiovascular system? | Finding: While there are some studies that suggest a possible link between vitamin K2-rich diets and higher vascular health. However, the studies are not very conclusive.

claim_topic: Can shoe insoles relieve pain in people with high arches?
evidence_text: Claim: Can shoe insoles relieve pain in people with high arches? | Finding: Shoe insoles are often prescribed for foot malpositions. However, there are hardly any good studies on the effectiveness of these remedies. So for the time being, it remains largely unclear what orthopedic shoe insoles can do for people with foot malpositions and whether they relieve pain in the long term.

claim_topic: Can shoe insoles relieve pain in people with foot deformities other than high arch?
evidence_text: Claim: Can shoe insoles relieve pain in people with foot deformities other than high arch? | Finding: Shoe insoles are often prescribed for foot malpositions. However, there are hardly any good studies on the effectiveness of these remedies. So for the time being, it remains largely unclear what orthopedic shoe insoles can do for people with foot malpositions and whether they relieve pain in the long term.

claim_topic: Can dowsers find harmful soil zones or water veins?
evidence_text: Claim: Can dowsers find harmful soil zones or water veins? | Finding: Small studies show that dowsing rods cannot detect water veins or hypothetical interference zones in the ground.

claim_topic: Does bioresonance therapy help with health complaints?
evidence_text: Claim: Does bioresonance therapy help with health complaints? | Finding: Good studies on the question are hard to find. Due to the lack of proof of efficacy, the risk of misdiagnosis and the lack of plausibility, professional associations have been warning against bioresonance for some time.

claim_topic: Do irradiations with cold red light help with chronic gingivitis?
evidence_text: Claim: Do irradiations with cold red light help with chronic gingivitis? | Finding: Previous studies indicate that chronic gingivitis and inflammation after dental surgery do not improve with irradiation with cold red light.

claim_topic: Does the Aspire system help you lose weight?
evidence_text: Claim: Does the Aspire system help you lose weight? | Finding: Although there is only one small study on this, it shows a very large effect - which indicates that it is effective.

claim_topic: Can FLEXISEQ ointment relieve osteoarthritis pain?
evidence_text: Claim: Can FLEXISEQ ointment relieve osteoarthritis pain? | Finding: Comparisons to date with other commonly used treatments are difficult to interpret but do not yield clear evidence of efficacy.

claim_topic: Can butterbur prevent migraine attacks?
evidence_text: Claim: Can butterbur prevent migraine attacks? | Finding: Two well-done randomized-controlled trials show efficacy - the number of migraine attacks can probably be reduced with butterbur. Even if the effect is not huge, taking it may be worthwhile due to only minor side effects.

claim_topic: Does bisphenol A trigger allergies?
evidence_text: Claim: Does bisphenol A trigger allergies? | Finding: Individual observational studies suggest an association between bisphenol A intake and the development of asthma, but not allergy, in early childhood. Asthma is often the consequence of allergy. However, the measurement of bisphenol A intake in these studies is too imprecise for a clear statement.

claim_topic: Can maggots accelerate the healing of chronic wounds compared to conventional treatment?
evidence_text: Claim: Can maggots accelerate the healing of chronic wounds compared to conventional treatment? | Finding: Maggot therapy may not heal chronic wounds any faster than conventional wound care. However, the maggots seem to be able to clean the wound of dead tissue more quickly - but also cause more pain.

claim_topic: Do electric toothbrushes protect oral health better than manual brushes?
evidence_text: Claim: Do electric toothbrushes protect oral health better than manual brushes? | Finding: Electric toothbrushes probably combat plaque and bleeding gums slightly better than conventional manual toothbrushes. The type of electric brush does not seem to play a major role.

claim_topic: Do antidepressants from the group of serotonin reuptake inhibitors help with depression?
evidence_text: Claim: Do antidepressants from the group of serotonin reuptake inhibitors help with depression? | Finding: Serotonin reuptake inhibitors have been shown to be helpful in more severe depression, although the exact mechanisms are not clear. Overall, very strong or rapid effects are not expected. For milder depression, efficacy is more debatable. Sometimes patients have to try several SSRI preparations until they feel an improvement in symptoms, and some sufferers are not helped by the drugs at all. Well-done studies should help clarify the situation in the future so that more targeted treatment is possible.

claim_topic: Is there a health risk from metal contaminants in lipsticks?
evidence_text: Claim: Is there a health risk from metal contaminants in lipsticks? | Finding: Several chemical analyses find traces of metals in lipsticks, which can in principle be harmful in high concentrations. However, the analyses do not examine the quantities in which the metals are actually absorbed and whether they cause damage in the body. Overall, there is still too little research into whether there could be a risk for some of the metal impurities if they are used very frequently.

claim_topic: Can topiramate reduce the frequency of migraine attacks?
evidence_text: Claim: Can topiramate reduce the frequency of migraine attacks? | Finding: Possibly yes. A review by the Cochrane Collaboration attests that topiramate slightly reduces the frequency of migraine attacks in adults, and in some patients the attacks even decrease significantly. Still, there are unanswered questions and the side effects should not be underestimated.

claim_topic: Does particulate matter pollution increase the risk of heart attack - even if the EU limits are complied with?
evidence_text: Claim: Does particulate matter pollution increase the risk of heart attack - even if the EU limits are complied with? | Finding: Recent studies from Europe indicate that everyday exposure to particulate matter may increase the risk of acute heart disease (myocardial infarction, angina pectoris). General mortality may also be increased already by 'allowed' long-term exposure within the current EU limits.

claim_topic: Are endocrine disruptors in cosmetics a health risk?
evidence_text: Claim: Are endocrine disruptors in cosmetics a health risk? | Finding: Although many cosmetics do indeed contain substances that can influence the hormone system, a health risk has not been proven. Ecological consequences, on the other hand, have already been demonstrated.

claim_topic: Can a dietary supplement containing omega-3 fatty acids, lipids, vitamins, and nutrients ("Souvenaid") noticeably slow or halt the decline of mental performance in Alzheimer's disease?
evidence_text: Claim: Can a dietary supplement containing omega-3 fatty acids, lipids, vitamins, and nutrients ("Souvenaid") noticeably slow or halt the decline of mental performance in Alzheimer's disease? | Finding: Three randomized-controlled trials show that such a dietary supplement (Souvenaid®) is unlikely to markedly slow or halt the progression of Alzheimer's dementia. Taking omega-3 fatty acid or vitamin B supplements alone also does not appear to have such an effect.

claim_topic: Do vitamin E supplements increase the likelihood of early death?
evidence_text: Claim: Do vitamin E supplements increase the likelihood of early death? | Finding: Studies on this topic are very inconsistent. Nevertheless, there is a possibility that vitamin E increases the risk of death. A meta-analysis warns against high-dose vitamin preparations.

claim_topic: Does meditation help against stress?
evidence_text: Claim: Does meditation help against stress? | Finding: Various forms of meditation seem to be able to alleviate stress both in healthy individuals and in people with mental illness. Studies on this are numerous, but the quality of the studies is consistently unsatisfactory.

claim_topic: Are there methods that effectively help against hormonal hair loss?
evidence_text: Claim: Are there methods that effectively help against hormonal hair loss? | Finding: Besides own hair transplantation, the active substances finasteride or minoxidil (as a solution) can help, but both agents have side effects. The effectiveness of other means is hardly or not secured.

claim_topic: Does eye training help prevent myopia?
evidence_text: Claim: Does eye training help prevent myopia? | Finding: According to the current state of studies, an effectiveness of eye training can only be expected for very few diseases; an effect as prevention or therapy against myopia cannot be assumed at present.

claim_topic: Does Cryolipolysis cause noticeable body fat reduction?
evidence_text: Claim: Does Cryolipolysis cause noticeable body fat reduction? | Finding: The effectiveness of cryolipolysis cannot be assessed objectively, as there are no scientific efficacy studies on it.

claim_topic: Is acupuncture for chronic pain more effective than placebo acupuncture treatment?
evidence_text: Claim: Is acupuncture for chronic pain more effective than placebo acupuncture treatment? | Finding: Acupuncture is slightly superior to sham acupuncture treatment for some types of pain. However, pain patients are unlikely to notice this difference.

claim_topic: Can Internet-based self-help training based on cognitive behavioral therapy reduce the burden of tinnitus?
evidence_text: Claim: Can Internet-based self-help training based on cognitive behavioral therapy reduce the burden of tinnitus? | Finding: Cognitive behavioral therapy can noticeably improve the quality of life and depressiveness of tinnitus sufferers. Internet-based self-help training based on cognitive behavioral therapy could be similarly helpful, but is often discontinued by sufferers.

claim_topic: Do probiotic foods have an antidepressant effect or a positive effect on the mind?
evidence_text: Claim: Do probiotic foods have an antidepressant effect or a positive effect on the mind? | Finding: Whether probiotics can help with depression or have a positive effect on the mood has never been investigated in clinical trials. In people with constipation, they could possibly improve mood.

claim_topic: Does treatment with radioactive agents help with pain in chronic inflammatory joint disease?
evidence_text: Claim: Does treatment with radioactive agents help with pain in chronic inflammatory joint disease? | Finding: Depending on the cause of the pain, radiosynoviorthesis can lead to considerable pain reduction, as confirmed by a 2009 review. However, it is not proven whether the treatment is more effective than cortisone treatment.

claim_topic: Does frequent porn use reduce gray matter volume in the brain?
evidence_text: Claim: Does frequent porn use reduce gray matter volume in the brain? | Finding: The study is not powered to examine the long-term effects of pornography on the brain and other studies on this were not found.

claim_topic: Can the active ingredient acetyl salicylic acid (ASA) protect against cancer?
evidence_text: Claim: Can the active ingredient acetyl salicylic acid (ASA) protect against cancer? | Finding: Taking ASA daily for several years seems to be able to reduce the risk of dying from cancer somewhat. However, it increases the risk of severe internal bleeding and stomach problems.

claim_topic: Is tick-borne tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) much milder in children than in adults?
evidence_text: Claim: Is tick-borne tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) much milder in children than in adults? | Finding: Current studies suggest that TBE is probably associated with milder symptoms in children than in adults. Permanent damage is also less frequent in younger patients. However, TBE can also have severe health consequences in children in individual cases.

claim_topic: Does treatment with cyanoacrylate (for example, Sapheon Venaseal™) help against varicose veins as well or better than other methods?
evidence_text: Claim: Does treatment with cyanoacrylate (for example, Sapheon Venaseal™) help against varicose veins as well or better than other methods? | Finding: To date, there are no results from clinical studies on this method. The efficacy in comparison with other treatments is therefore unclear.

claim_topic: Did oseltamivir (Tamiflu®) or other neuraminidase inhibitors help reduce deaths from the H1N1 influenza virus ("swine flu" virus)?
evidence_text: Claim: Did oseltamivir (Tamiflu®) or other neuraminidase inhibitors help reduce deaths from the H1N1 influenza virus ("swine flu" virus)? | Finding: Previously published analyses of data from the H1N1 influenza ("swine flu") pandemic period are of insufficient quality to answer this question.

claim_topic: Is aluminum intake responsible for the development of Alzheimer's disease?
evidence_text: Claim: Is aluminum intake responsible for the development of Alzheimer's disease? | Finding: Scientific studies cannot prove with certainty a connection between the metal aluminum and the disease Alzheimer, but they cannot exclude it either.

claim_topic: Can regular exercise prevent or relieve migraine symptoms?
evidence_text: Claim: Can regular exercise prevent or relieve migraine symptoms? | Finding: In some, but not all, studies, regular exercise seems to at least somewhat reduce the pain intensity of future migraine attacks. Whether the frequency of migraine attacks can also be reduced cannot be assessed with certainty. for this, larger, better validated studies would have to be conducted.

claim_topic: Does less than 7h of sleep daily increase mental performance?
evidence_text: Claim: Does less than 7h of sleep daily increase mental performance? | Finding: Two small randomized-controlled studies indicate that mental performance decreases with the number of sleepless hours per night and the number of nights with insufficient sleep. No single scientific study provides evidence of an increase in mental performance due to shorter sleep duration.

claim_topic: Does regular intake of extra virgin olive oil protect against coronary heart disease such as heart attack?
evidence_text: Claim: Does regular intake of extra virgin olive oil protect against coronary heart disease such as heart attack? | Finding: Regular consumption of cold-pressed olive oil may possibly prevent coronary heart disease. However, direct evidence is still pending.

claim_topic: Do frequent ejaculations have a protective effect against prostate cancer?
evidence_text: Claim: Do frequent ejaculations have a protective effect against prostate cancer? | Finding: A cohort study suggests that more frequent ejaculations starting at age 40, or over a lifetime, could potentially lower the risk of prostate cancer. This is not exclusive to ejaculations from masturbation, but from any sexual activity.

claim_topic: Does condom use cause depression in women?
evidence_text: Claim: Does condom use cause depression in women? | Finding: A study examining exactly this question was not found. Some scientific works with a broad question rather lead to the conclusion that there is no connection between depression and condom use.

claim_topic: Do today's children have a shorter life expectancy than their parents?
evidence_text: Claim: Do today's children have a shorter life expectancy than their parents? | Finding: Obesity and physical inactivity are increasing risk factors worldwide that can shorten life. In 2005, a study from the USA concluded that life expectancy could be reduced by 3 to 9 months when these risks were included.

claim_topic: Do rising temperatures and CO2 levels increase the risk of pollen allergy?
evidence_text: Claim: Do rising temperatures and CO2 levels increase the risk of pollen allergy? | Finding: Rising temperatures and increased CO2 concentrations cause plants to produce larger amounts of pollen over a longer period of time. However, it is unclear whether larger amounts of pollen and a longer pollen season increase the likelihood of developing pollen allergy.

claim_topic: Does training on vibration platforms cause a noticeable buildup of muscle strength?
evidence_text: Claim: Does training on vibration platforms cause a noticeable buildup of muscle strength? | Finding: Vibration training may be helpful for building muscle strength in the legs, but it is not better than conventional training for this purpose. Whether the method is also suitable for weight reduction has not been sufficiently studied.

claim_topic: Does glucosamine prolong life?
evidence_text: Claim: Does glucosamine prolong life? | Finding: Although research here is still in its infancy and there is only one cohort study in humans besides basic studies, this shows possible effects. Further studies with better methods and other groups of participants are necessary.

claim_topic: Does Kinesio tape help in the treatment of joint and muscle injuries?
evidence_text: Claim: Does Kinesio tape help in the treatment of joint and muscle injuries? | Finding: There is no evidence that kinesio tape can reduce pain within a few days. It is unclear whether taping can help improve movement restrictions caused by an injury.

claim_topic: Do injections with Botulinum Toxin A (Botox®) help with urinary incontinence?
evidence_text: Claim: Do injections with Botulinum Toxin A (Botox®) help with urinary incontinence? | Finding: Several small randomized-controlled trials show that injections of botulinum toxin A into the detrusor muscle surrounding the urinary bladder can reduce, but not completely prevent, the incidence of involuntary urinary leakage.

claim_topic: Can apigenin reduce cancer risk or prevent cancer progression?
evidence_text: Claim: Can apigenin reduce cancer risk or prevent cancer progression? | Finding: Studies suggest that even high levels of apigenin in food do not protect against cancer. In individual cases, it is suspected that apigenin in high amounts could weaken the effect of chemotherapy or even accelerate cancer growth.

claim_topic: Do generic drugs work as well as original drugs?
evidence_text: Claim: Do generic drugs work as well as original drugs? | Finding: Yes, the summarized results of clinical studies do not provide any evidence for a poorer efficacy of generics compared to originator drugs. However, comparative studies exist only for some agents against cardiovascular diseases and epilepsy.

claim_topic: Are animal-assisted therapies effective for mental illness?
evidence_text: Claim: Are animal-assisted therapies effective for mental illness? | Finding: Studies on the effects of animal-assisted therapies are only partially conclusive. It seems plausible that animal-assisted therapies can be supportive for some mental illnesses; however, very large or rapid effects are unlikely.

claim_topic: Can lack of sleep cause obesity?
evidence_text: Claim: Can lack of sleep cause obesity? | Finding: People who regularly get too little sleep may be more likely to be overweight than those who get enough sleep. But whether lack of sleep itself causes obesity is unclear.

claim_topic: Is breaking an energy-saving lamp harmful to health?
evidence_text: Claim: Is breaking an energy-saving lamp harmful to health? | Finding: If an energy-saving lamp breaks, mercury vapor is released in quantities that can exceed the limits considered safe. Whether this can cause damage to health has not been directly investigated. However, after removal of the broken glass and good ventilation of the room, the value quickly falls back below the limit value.

claim_topic: Does copper intake increase the risk of Alzheimer's disease?
evidence_text: Claim: Does copper intake increase the risk of Alzheimer's disease? | Finding: Some studies claim to have found links between high copper levels and Alzheimer's disease. Whether copper intake actually has an impact on Alzheimer's risk is not clear.

claim_topic: Do air ions cause an improvement of allergies?
evidence_text: Claim: Do air ions cause an improvement of allergies? | Finding: Whether ionized air can reduce allergic symptoms is unclear, as no studies exist on this question. Air ionization devices do not appear to be effective against asthma in general.

claim_topic: Do air ions cause an improvement of asthma??
evidence_text: Claim: Do air ions cause an improvement of asthma?? | Finding: Whether ionized air can reduce allergic symptoms is unclear, as no studies exist on this question. Air ionization devices do not appear to be effective against asthma in general.

claim_topic: Do smoking bans lead to fewer preterm births?
evidence_text: Claim: Do smoking bans lead to fewer preterm births? | Finding: A large review shows a 10% reduced risk of preterm birth. Due to some limitations, the evidence is nevertheless low, further studies from different countries will probably soon bring clarity.

claim_topic: Do special garments with the active ingredient Liporeductyl help against cellulite?
evidence_text: Claim: Do special garments with the active ingredient Liporeductyl help against cellulite? | Finding: There are only small studies that neither stand up to methodological criteria nor have been scientifically published. Sustained efficacy has not been proven, which, according to the current status, applies to all common remedies against cellulite.

claim_topic: Does alcohol in moderate amounts prolong life?
evidence_text: Claim: Does alcohol in moderate amounts prolong life? | Finding: In moderate amounts, alcohol could reduce the likelihood of dying prematurely. In higher doses, however, it clearly increases this risk. This is unclear for caffeine.

claim_topic: Does caffeine make us die sooner???
evidence_text: Claim: Does caffeine make us die sooner??? | Finding: In moderate amounts, alcohol could reduce the likelihood of dying prematurely. In higher doses, however, it clearly increases this risk. This is unclear for caffeine.

claim_topic: Does light freezing help with weight loss?
evidence_text: Claim: Does light freezing help with weight loss? | Finding: Some laboratory studies show that the body reacts to colder temperatures with higher energy consumption and burns more fat. Nevertheless, it is completely unclear whether this supports weight loss; that is, whether the process is strong enough and whether other mechanisms do not work against it. Weight loss through freezing has not been investigated in clinical studies.

claim_topic: Does acupuncture help against hay fever?
evidence_text: Claim: Does acupuncture help against hay fever? | Finding: We have not found any meaningful studies that can provide evidence of improvement in hay fever.

claim_topic: Do earrings cause discomfort by destroying acupuncture points or meridians?
evidence_text: Claim: Do earrings cause discomfort by destroying acupuncture points or meridians? | Finding: Earrings very often lead to complications, fortunately most of them are harmless. However, whether earrings can also destroy meridians or similar representation points of body regions in the auricle and thus lead to health complaints has not been investigated in studies.

claim_topic: Does the "Rolfing" treatment cause an improvement of body malpositions as well as certain pains?
